title: Restoration of adult human central nervous system circuitry after injury

concept.text: The proposed innovation is the restoration of working neural connections in the adult human brain or spinal cord after injury. It would repair the circuitry needed for signals to travel through damaged tissue and produce useful function. A demanding example would be a person with chronic, clinically complete spinal cord injury recovering walking, sensation and continence through functional reconnection across the injury.

The therapeutic gap is documented for spinal cord injury. The supplied July 2026 trial abstract describes severe, irreversible motor and sensory deficits and states that damaged neural circuitry remains beyond the restorative capabilities of available therapies. The broader concept encompasses reconstruction of connections and, where needed, replacement and functional integration of lost neurons. Those components describe the intended capability. The supplied evidence leaves the extent of spontaneous axonal repair and neuronal replacement across different adult central nervous system regions unresolved.

significance.text: Durable recovery of walking and sensation through demonstrated reconstruction across a chronic spinal cord injury would create a major clinical capability. The July 2026 report grounds the need by describing lasting motor and sensory deficits and an unmet circuit-restoration goal. Achieving the proposed capability could restore voluntary function in people whose damaged connections currently prevent it.

Conditional impact assessment. Recovery of continence and other autonomic functions would broaden the benefit beyond mobility, potentially improving independence and reducing daily care requirements. The original research also identifies bowel, bladder and sexual function as important consequences of spinal cord injury. The supplied abstract provides insufficient detail to substantiate those consequences for its participants or establish which autonomic functions a repair treatment could recover.

Conditional extension. Successful spinal cord reconstruction could motivate repair approaches for chronic focal brain injuries, including injuries caused by stroke or trauma. Each application would require evidence that treatment reconstructs the relevant connections and restores their functions. The supplied evidence leaves recovery trajectories after stroke and traumatic brain injury unresolved, including how recovery changes after the acute period.

Scope assessment. Repairing a focal injury would establish a capability whose applicability to diffuse, ongoing neurodegeneration would require separate demonstration. Alzheimer’s disease adds the challenge of a distributed disease process and continuing damage. Similarly, success in one spinal injury population would establish demonstrated clinical breadth within that population, with additional evidence needed for other lesion locations, severities and causes.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is reliable, treatment-caused reconstruction of functional adult human central nervous system circuitry after injury. The July 2026 transplantation report documents this therapeutic goal while providing preliminary safety and exploratory functional observations. Its expectation that transplanted cells will engraft and differentiate describes a proposed mechanism. Demonstrated reconstruction of human circuitry remains an additional evidentiary requirement.

Engineering synthesis. A successful intervention would need to establish viable neural connections through or around damaged tissue, connect appropriate upstream and downstream partners, and integrate those connections into coordinated activity. Where neuronal replacement contributes, the replacement cells would need to survive, acquire suitable functions and participate in useful networks. These are functional requirements inferred from the proposed innovation. The supplied abstract leaves their relative difficulty and the best biological route unresolved.

Engineering synthesis. Repair would also need sufficient specificity to support useful movement, interpretable sensation and appropriate autonomic control. Practical development would require durable function, manageable treatment and rehabilitation burdens, and safety across the intended patient population. For cell-based approaches, sustained surveillance for tumors and graft-related adverse events would remain important. The four-person observations provide an initial safety experience with limited coverage of uncommon or delayed outcomes.

Attribution synthesis. Clinical completeness describes the findings of a neurological examination and leaves open the possibility of anatomically spared pathways. Recovery could involve recruitment or recovery of such pathways. Establishing reconstruction therefore requires convergent evidence connecting the intervention, newly functional connections and recovered abilities. Stimulator-independent gains and connectivity measurements each contribute evidence, while their interpretation depends on a study design capable of distinguishing these mechanisms.

current_state.text: Sugai and colleagues reported a first-in-human, open-label phase 1 study of induced pluripotent stem-cell-derived neural stem/progenitor cell transplantation in Nature Medicine on 21 July 2026, with a September 2026 issue date. Four patients with subacute cervical complete spinal cord injury received transplants. The supplied abstract presents circuit restoration as an unmet therapeutic goal.

No tumor formation or graft-related adverse events were observed during 2–4 years of follow-up. At week 52, median motor-score improvement was 13 points relative to a baseline measured two weeks after injury. Two participants changed from American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale grade A to grades C and D, respectively. These observations describe a small early clinical experience, with efficacy assessed exploratorily.

The reported gains were numerically greater than spontaneous recovery in a registry-based comparison cohort. That comparison provides context, while the four-person, open-label, nonrandomized design leaves treatment attribution uncertain. Subacute recovery remains a competing explanation. The observations leave both treatment-caused functional recovery and reconstruction of connections across the injury unresolved.

The supplied evidence review covered the PubMed abstract and available figure captions. Access to the full article and figure images remains outside that review. A caption describes expected engraftment and differentiation of transplanted cells at the injury site, leaving direct demonstration of the proposed mechanism unresolved. The source record lists no extraction problems, but the accessible material still limits assessment of methods, participant-level outcomes and mechanistic evidence.

Evidence limitation. The earlier research describes electrical stimulation producing assisted movement in small studies and attributes this to recruitment of remaining circuits. The supplied review contains no inspected clinical stimulation studies, so the extent of those achievements and the mechanisms responsible remain unverified within this record. Functional gains during stimulation, persistent gains after stimulation and evidence of reconstructed connections require separate assessment.

Coverage limitation. The documented clinical observations are anchored to the July 2026 publication. Although the source was retrieved on 1 November 2026, the supplied record contains no completed freshness search establishing the field’s comprehensive status on that date. Later developments and additional relevant studies remain outside the evidence assembled here.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration. People with chronic, motor-and-sensory-complete spinal cord injury regain independent overground walking, meaningful sensation below the lesion and continence. The protocol should prospectively define chronicity, neurological completeness, independent walking, meaningful sensation, continence and the duration required for a durable gain. These endpoints constitute a deliberately demanding proposal for this concept.
completion_criteria.label: Independent walking, sensation and continence return after chronic complete spinal injury

completion_criteria.text: Proposed mechanistic demonstration. Recovered abilities persist after any implanted stimulator is switched off, with the duration and conditions of stimulation withdrawal specified in advance. Convergent imaging and physiology, interpreted alongside the clinical outcomes, should establish new functional connectivity across the injury. The study should distinguish reconstruction from recruitment or recovery of spared pathways and assess how strongly each measurement supports that attribution.
completion_criteria.label: New functional connectivity across injury sustains recovery without stimulation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed study design. A prospectively specified comparator, repeated baseline assessments and standardized rehabilitation would help distinguish treatment effects from spontaneous recovery, training and measurement variation. The registry comparison in the July 2026 trial illustrates the relevance of spontaneous recovery to interpreting subacute gains. Demonstrations confined to subacute injury would establish results in that setting, with a separate chronic-injury demonstration required for the proposed scope.
completion_criteria.label: Prospective controlled comparisons distinguish chronic injury treatment effects from confounds

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries. Convincing completion would include replicated results across independent teams or sites, sustained follow-up and enough participants to characterize the reliability of benefit and important harms. Reports should specify injury level, severity, time since injury, anatomical features, treatment burden, rehabilitation requirements and residual limitations. Finite trials would establish demonstrated breadth across those conditions. Broader applicability would require further evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication characterizes durable benefits, harms and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis. CLM-03, Arrest and recovery of function in symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease, overlaps in its goal of recovering central nervous system function. CLM-04 focuses on circuitry damaged by injury. CLM-03 additionally entails addressing a diffuse neurodegenerative disease process. Transfer of a repair method between these settings remains conditional on disease-specific evidence.

Roster-based synthesis. CLM-06, Therapeutic remuscularization of the adult human heart, and CLM-15, Restoration of nephron number in the adult human kidney, share the broader ambition of restoring functional tissue within an adult organ. Their defining functional units are cardiac muscle and nephrons, respectively. CLM-04 requires neural connections to integrate into circuits that carry appropriate signals and support coordinated behavior.

Roster-based synthesis. CLM-05, Durable organ xenotransplantation at clinical scale, and CLM-11, Implantable human-scale organs assembled outside the body, concern replacement organs and their clinical integration. CLM-04 concerns repair of existing central nervous system circuitry. Cell transplantation could contribute to that repair, while its success would depend on the neural function restored within the recipient’s circuitry.

Roster-based synthesis. CLM-12, Selective, durable control of pathological chronic pain, overlaps through neural function, sensory processing and possible neuromodulatory approaches. Its defining outcome is durable control of pathological pain. CLM-04 requires evidence of reconstructed injury-damaged circuitry and recovered function. Pain outcomes could form part of the benefit and safety assessment of a repair intervention.

change_log.change: Preserved CLM-04’s identity and broad adult central nervous system repair scope while anchoring the documented therapeutic gap to spinal cord injury.
change_log.reason: The supplied abstract supports the spinal cord restoration goal, with broader brain-repair applications remaining conditional.

change_log.change: Qualified absolute statements about spontaneous axonal repair, neuronal replacement and electrical stimulation mechanisms.
change_log.reason: The inspected evidence leaves those broader biological claims unresolved. Their evidentiary limits do not invalidate the innovation.

change_log.change: Expanded the trial account with its publication date, open-label design, exact baseline timing, graft-related safety observations, AIS conversions and registry comparison.
change_log.reason: These details preserve the supported quantitative findings and improve interpretation of the exploratory outcomes.

change_log.change: Distinguished reported functional improvement, expected graft behavior and demonstrated circuit reconstruction.
change_log.reason: The reviewed abstract and captions establish observations and expectations while leaving treatment causality and reconstructed connectivity unresolved.

change_log.change: Strengthened the proposed completion criteria with prospective definitions, mechanistic attribution, reproducibility and practical boundaries.
change_log.reason: Clinical completeness and stimulator-independent gains alone leave spared-pathway explanations open. The thresholds remain proposals.

change_log.change: Qualified detailed autonomic consequences and removed the categorical claim that stroke and traumatic brain injury deficits become fixed after an acute window.
change_log.reason: The supplied source does not establish those broader factual assertions. Autonomic recovery remains an explicit proposed benefit.

change_log.change: Retained the related CLM mappings and added relevant overlap with chronic pain control.
change_log.reason: The supplied concept roster establishes the identifiers and titles, resolving the review’s concern about undocumented mappings.

change_log.change: Preserved full-article access limitations, the absence of reviewed stimulation trials and the unassessed freshness of field-wide coverage.
change_log.reason: These limitations affect the scope of interpretation while preserving the supported July 2026 observations.

unresolved_issues: The extent to which the reported motor gains resulted from transplantation, spontaneous recovery, rehabilitation or other factors remains unresolved.
The supplied evidence leaves graft survival, differentiation, functional integration and reconstructed connectivity in the treated participants unresolved.
The full article and figure images were outside the supplied review, limiting assessment of methods and participant-level evidence.
Clinical stimulation achievements and their mechanisms require source-specific assessment beyond the supplied record.
Chronicity, meaningful sensation, continence, durability and the evidence needed to distinguish reconstructed from spared connections require prospective operational definitions.
Applicability across chronic spinal injury populations and to focal brain injuries remains to be demonstrated.
Longer-term safety and the frequency of uncommon adverse outcomes remain uncertain after a four-person study.
The supplied record does not establish comprehensive field-wide status as of 1 November 2026 or later.
The review’s reservation about other CLM identifier mappings was resolved using the supplied roster. All other substantive correction recommendations were incorporated.

brief.title: Repair of damaged connections in the brain and spinal cord
possible: People living with paralysis after a spinal injury could regain independent walking, useful sensation and bladder and bowel control. Repair would restore working nerve connections so signals could cross the damaged area and support lasting recovery.
Repairing connections in the adult brain could also restore abilities lost after a stroke or traumatic injury.
why: Recovering movement, feeling and control of bodily functions could give people more independence and reduce the daily care they need. The benefit would extend beyond mobility to activities they currently rely on others to manage.

sources.who: Keiko Sugai, Osahiko Tsuji and colleagues
sources.showed: Four people with recent, severe neck-level spinal injuries received transplants of cells capable of developing into nerve cells. Movement scores improved, and no tumors or transplant-related adverse events were observed during follow-up.
sources.quote: These gains were numerically greater than spontaneous recovery observed in a registry-based cohort.
sources.cited_for: The study provides early human safety observations and movement gains after nerve-cell transplantation.
sources.not_established: The small, nonrandomized study did not establish that transplantation caused recovery or rebuilt connections across the injury.

sources.who: Joel R. Martin and colleagues at the University of California, San Diego
sources.showed: After nerve-forming cell transplants for longstanding spinal injuries, two participants had lasting improvements in movement and sensation scores and measurable muscle activity. These changes did not produce useful functional recovery.
sources.quote: All subjects tolerated the procedure well with no serious adverse events (SAEs) in the immediate post-procedure period.
sources.cited_for: Long-term follow-up shows that measurable neurological gains can occur without useful recovery.
sources.not_established: The uncontrolled study did not demonstrate restored independence or reconstructed connections across the injury.

sources.who: Henri Lorach, Andrea Galvez and colleagues
sources.showed: An implanted digital link connected brain signals to spinal stimulation, helping one participant stand and walk. After rehabilitation, he could also walk with crutches while the system was off.
sources.quote: The participant regained the ability to walk with crutches overground even when the BSI was switched off.
sources.cited_for: Walking gains can persist without active stimulation after rehabilitation supported by an implanted system.
sources.not_established: The participant retained some spinal connections; walking with the system off did not establish newly reconstructed pathways.

sources.who: Edelle C. Field-Fote and Kathryn E. Roach
sources.showed: A randomized trial compared walking-training approaches in people with longstanding spinal injuries who retained some movement. Walking speed improved, and training over ground produced greater distance gains than treadmill training.
sources.quote: In people with chronic motor incomplete SCI, walking speed improved with both overground training and treadmill-based training; however, walking distance improved to a greater extent with overground training.
sources.cited_for: Rehabilitation itself can improve walking, so repair trials need comparisons that account for training.
sources.not_established: The trial did not test reconstruction of damaged connections or recovery after complete loss of movement and sensation.

shown: Sugai and colleagues reported improved movement scores after cell transplantation in people with recent spinal injuries. Martin and colleagues found lasting changes in movement and sensation tests after longstanding injuries, without useful functional recovery.

Lorach and colleagues enabled a participant with a longstanding, partially preserved spinal injury to walk using a digital link between brain signals and spinal stimulation. He later walked with crutches with the system switched off.
missing: People with longstanding spinal injuries and no detectable movement or sensation have yet to regain independent walking, useful feeling and continence.
New working connections across an injury have yet to be convincingly linked to recovered abilities.
Independent teams have yet to reproduce reliable, lasting repair while establishing important harms and treatment burdens.

milestones.label: Walking, sensation and continence return after longstanding complete injury
milestones.explanation: People with longstanding spinal injuries and no detectable movement or sensation would have to regain independent walking, useful feeling and bladder and bowel control durably. This would establish recovery that changes daily life.

milestones.label: New connections sustain recovery with stimulation switched off
milestones.explanation: Recovery would have to persist without stimulation, with imaging and electrical tests showing new working connections across the injury rather than use of surviving pathways. This would establish reconstruction as the cause.

milestones.label: Controlled comparisons establish treatment effects in longstanding injury
milestones.explanation: A study planned in advance would need comparison groups, repeated starting measurements and standardized rehabilitation in longstanding injury. This would separate treatment effects from recovery, training and measurement variation.

milestones.label: Independent replication establishes lasting benefits and practical limits
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce lasting benefits with enough participants and follow-up to assess important harms, injury differences and treatment burdens. This would establish reliability and who can benefit.

uncertain: The transplant studies leave open how much improvement came from treatment, natural recovery or rehabilitation.
A complete loss of movement and sensation on examination can coexist with surviving nerve pathways, complicating proof of reconstruction.
The required duration of recovery and thresholds for useful sensation and continence remain to be defined.

page.title: Functional regeneration of adult human central nervous system circuits
page.definition: An intervention biologically rebuilds connections in an injured adult human brain or spinal cord, restoring a lost function through those connections. Rebuilding may involve regrowth of axons, the signal-carrying fibres of neurons, or integration of replacement neurons.

goal.need: WHO's global estimates quantify the burden of spinal cord injury, one population addressed by circuit repair. The resulting disabilities can affect walking, hand use and bowel or bladder emptying. The prevalence figures do not establish eligibility for any particular regenerative treatment.

figures.caption: Global burden of spinal cord injury in 2021
rows: People living with spinal cord injury
figures.note: Years lived with disability measures population health loss; it is not a count of people.

statements.quote: SCI is a major cause of long-term disability

statements.body: US Department of Veterans Affairs, Office of Research and Development
statements.quote: Researchers are pursuing new methods to repair damage to the spinal cord and restore function after SCI.

completion.title: Biologically reconstructed human neural circuits cause recovery of a lost function.
completion.criterion: In a specified adult injury population, a controlled confirmatory clinical study meets its prospectively defined functional endpoint and demonstrates that newly formed biological neural connections mediate the recovered function. Anatomical and physiological evidence distinguishes reconstruction from recruitment of spared pathways. The protocol specifies the injury population, comparator, required functional effect, follow-up and statistical success rule. Completion is established only for the population studied.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; provisional synthesis because no shared external completion criterion was identified.
completion.basis: Searches of ICCP trial guidance, ISSCR translation guidance, CNS regeneration criteria, FDA material and NINDS priorities found no shared human circuit-reconstruction test. This fallback joins controlled functional benefit to mechanistic attribution. Sugai et al. could not directly demonstrate graft integration. The brain–spine interface study restored walking in one participant without establishing biological reconstruction.

milestones.title: Severed axons in an adult mammalian CNS injury grow into or beyond the lesion.
milestones.criterion: Axons demonstrably originating from injured neurons extend into or beyond the lesion, with evidence excluding spared fibres as their source. This establishes anatomical regeneration without requiring functional recovery. Squair et al., published on 21 September 2023, reported directed regeneration across anatomically complete spinal cord injuries in mice. Their walking comparison included six mice per treated group and five each in uninjured and injury-only groups; selective inactivation experiments used five mice per group.
milestones.set_by: Axon-regeneration research convention, articulated by Tuszynski and Steward in Neuron in 2012; discussed principally for spinal cord injury.
milestones.threshold_quote: growth of a cut axon, and 2) extension into or beyond a lesion.

milestones.title: A candidate circuit-repair cell therapy demonstrates preclinical safety and efficacy.
milestones.criterion: Preclinical studies establish safety and efficacy before human administration, using models relevant to the intended injury and assessing delivery-related risks and tumorigenicity. ISSCR specifies no universal animal number or follow-up duration. One product-specific safety result appears in PMDA's 2024 SB623 dossier: rats receiving 500,000 cells were observed for 52 weeks, with four deaths among 39 treated animals and five among 34 vehicle controls. Deaths were attributed to administration techniques rather than the test substance.
milestones.set_by: International Society for Stem Cell Research, 2025 Guidelines, recommendation 3.3.1.2; applies to cell-based interventions across the injury cases.
milestones.threshold_quote: Early phase human studies should be preceded by a rigorous demonstration of safety and efficacy in preclinical studies.

milestones.title: An adult receives a biological circuit-repair treatment in a phase 1 safety study.
milestones.criterion: Human dosing occurs with protocol-defined safety follow-up. On 21 July 2026, Sugai et al. reported four subacute cervical spinal cord injury recipients: no tumors or graft-related adverse events over 2–4 years. Martin et al. reported four chronic thoracic injury recipients on 17 December 2024: 65 adverse events and one sepsis death after a sacral ulcer at 30 months; neurological gains produced no functional improvement. PISCES treated 11 men with chronic ischaemic stroke: no cell-related or immunological adverse events over 2 years. These are exposure and safety observations, not controlled efficacy evidence.
milestones.set_by: International Campaign for Cures of Spinal Cord Injury Paralysis panel, clinical trial design guidelines, Phase 1; written for spinal cord injury.
milestones.threshold_quote: first administration of the therapeutic intervention

milestones.title: A repair intervention produces a positive neurological outcome against controls in a phase 2 study.
milestones.criterion: A phase 2 study finds a positive change in a relevant outcome, using controls and blinded assessment. In STEMTRA, 63 adults with chronic traumatic brain injury were randomized and 61 underwent surgery: 46 received SB623 and 15 sham surgery. The week-24 Fugl–Meyer Motor Scale difference was 6.0 points (95% CI 0.3–11.8; p=0.0401). This measures motor impairment, not reconstructed connections. Sugai's uncontrolled median motor-score increase of 13 points at week 52 does not meet this controlled test.
milestones.set_by: International Campaign for Cures of Spinal Cord Injury Paralysis panel, clinical trial design guidelines, Phase 2; written for spinal cord injury.
milestones.threshold_quote: a positive change in relevant outcome variables

milestones.title: A repair intervention shows statistically significant clinical benefit in a multicentre confirmatory study.
milestones.criterion: A confirmatory study establishes clinical benefit across multiple centres and an acceptable adverse-event profile. Effect size, statistical significance and follow-up follow the study protocol; ICCP supplies no universal numerical recovery threshold. Mechanistic proof remains a separate requirement for completion. For traumatic brain injury, PMDA's review dated 8 October 2025 retains requirements for post-marketing assessment of Akuugo and collection of information reflecting its mechanism of action.
milestones.set_by: International Campaign for Cures of Spinal Cord Injury Paralysis panel, clinical trial design guidelines, Phase 3; written for spinal cord injury.

not_found: The retrieved human studies did not establish that newly formed biological connections caused the reported recovery.
Case-specific attainment of the anatomical regeneration criterion was not established for stroke or traumatic brain injury by the sources examined.
NINDS repair-priorities pages could not be retrieved because access returned HTTP 403.

results.finding: Four patients received iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells, with no tumors or graft-related adverse events over 2–4 years.
results.detail: The phase 1 study included scheduled safety follow-up.
results.quote: Here we report results from a first-in-human, open-label study of iPSC-NS/PC transplantation in four patients with subacute cervical complete SCI. The primary safety end point was achieved, with no tumor formation or graft-related adverse events observed during 2-4 years of follow-up and stable graft sites on imaging.

results.finding: Four treated patients had a median motor-score improvement of 13 points at week 52.
results.detail: This was an open-label phase 1 study, with an exploratory outcome and a historical registry comparison; it was not a controlled, blinded phase 2 study.
results.quote: Median improvement in the International Standards for Neurological Classification of Spinal Cord Injury motor score from baseline (2 weeks after injury) to week 52 was 13 points (range 10-40), with two patients improving in American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (grade A → C and A → D).

results.finding: Four adults with chronic thoracic spinal cord injury received NSI-566; 65 adverse events were recorded.
results.detail: The phase 1 safety study specified follow-up to 60 months. One participant died of sepsis related to a sacral ulcer at 30 months; immunosuppression could not be ruled out as a contributor.
results.quote: There were 65 adverse events recorded, but only one SAE in the four transplanted patients (0.25 SAEs per patient).

results.finding: In 30 mice with complete spinal cord injury, axons regenerated to their lumbar target region over two segments distally.
results.detail: The authors report regeneration in all mice across five cohorts. Anatomically complete injuries and tracing of neurons above the injury support the conclusion that the axons were regenerated rather than spared.
results.quote:
Replacing biomaterial depots with
lentivirus-mediated GDNF expression enabled
an extensive regrowth of axons to their natural
target region over two segments distally

results.finding: In one adult mouse with a cortical stab injury, 7 of 36 traced severed serotonin axon ends grew completely across the lesion.
results.detail: Time-lapse imaging traced regrowth to severed ends. The 36 ends were from an exemplar mouse; the stab-lesion imaging group included six mice.

results.finding: In spinal cord-injured mice, hiPSC-NS/PC transplantation (n=8; controls n=10) significantly improved motor recovery by day 49.
results.detail: The study also reports no tumor formation in representative spinal cord tissue and safety observations in mice. It does not report a preclinical assessment of delivery-related risks, so the full criterion is not established.
results.quote: Compared with control animals (n = 10), which received an injection of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), the transplanted mice showed significant recovery of motor function by 49 days post-injury (

results.finding: AST-OPC1 cervical spinal cord injury studies found no teratomas in 237 treated rats and 31 controls.
results.detail: Treated rats also showed improved locomotor performance versus vehicle controls (16 per group). Nine-month safety studies assessed administration, biodistribution and tumorigenicity; human-derived ectopic tissue occurred in 11 of 237 treated rats without associated adverse clinical signs.
results.quote: Out of 31 HBSS‐treated animals and 237 AST‐OPC1‐treated animals, no teratomas or mineralization were observed in the spinal cord or brain of any animal, consistent with prior safety testing of AST‐OPC1 in thoracic SCI

results.finding: CTX0E03 preclinical tumorigenicity studies: 0 reported treatment-related tumor pathologies; sample size not stated.
results.detail: The protocol also reports functional improvements in a rat ischemic stroke model and no cell-related adverse events in toxicity studies. It does not provide sample sizes, detailed delivery-risk results, or enough study methods to establish the full criterion.
results.quote:
No incidence of CTX0E03-related tumor pathologies have been found including in animals treated with 
tamoxifen, and where CTX0E03 cells survived, albeit at low numbers, for extended periods of time.

results.finding: PISCES treated 11 men with chronic ischaemic stroke and followed safety for 2 years.
results.detail: No immunological or cell-related adverse events were observed during the 2-year follow-up. Other adverse events were attributed to the procedure or comorbidities. The open-label study had no control group.

results.finding: Ten adults with severe traumatic brain injury received NSC-like cells; no serious adverse events were reported during 180-day follow-up.
results.detail: The phase I study used protocol-defined safety assessments. It had no control group and did not establish that the cells rebuilt neural circuits or caused functional recovery.
results.quote: Serial clinical, laboratory and radiographic evaluations demonstrated no mortality or serious adverse events during the transplantation procedure or during the follow-up period (180 days).

results.finding: In 36 ischemic stroke patients completing follow-up, sovateltide was associated with a reported 28-percentage-point advantage in Barthel Index improvement.
results.detail: The exploratory phase 2 trial was randomized, placebo-controlled and double-blind; 40 patients were randomized. The paper reports 64% versus 36% for a ≥40-point improvement, but these figures appear to represent shares of responders rather than within-group response rates. It did not establish reconstruction of human neural connections.
results.quote: Significantly more patients in the sovateltide group had an improved Barthel Index (BI) score of ≥ 40 points at 90 days of follow up (64 vs. 36% in the control group).

results.finding: STEMTRA: 61 adults with chronic TBI had a 6.0-point greater week-24 motor-score improvement with SB623 than sham surgery.
results.detail: The trial was randomized, sham-controlled and double-blind. The motor scale measures impairment; the study does not establish that connections were reconstructed.
results.quote: Intraparenchymal implantation of SB623 cells was safe and significantly improved motor status at 24 weeks in participants with chronic motor deficits after TBI, with continued improvement of function and ADL at 48 weeks.

results.finding: In 158 patients with acute ischaemic stroke, sovateltide increased the proportion with a good functional outcome at 90 days by 22.67 percentage points.
results.detail: The randomised, controlled phase III trial ran at 18 centres in India. The 95% confidence interval for the mRS outcome excluded no effect; adverse events were reported as unrelated to the drug. Neural repair is a proposed mechanism and remains a separate requirement for completion.
